title: Two-tier thickness perturbation on 22-layer ZnS/MgF2 alternating IR filter
scientific_hypothesis: A two-tier perturbation scheme with ±3% noise on layers 1-12 and ±12% independent perturbation on layers 13-22 will produce higher target scores than uniform perturbation by decoupling fine-scale phase matching from spectral envelope shaping.
design_principle: Quarter-wave stacks create stopbands through constructive interference of reflections; passbands emerge from defects or envelope modulation. The first half of the stack controls fine interference phase relationships while the second half shapes the broader spectral envelope. Recalled from standard thin-film interference theory.
proposed_topology: Air | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | Daimon-20 substrate (22 layers total, alternating high/low index)
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses with two-tier perturbation: layers 1-12 constrained to ±3% around 478.0/815.0 nm baseline, layers 13-22 allowed ±12% independent variation
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm band
maximize mean transmittance in 4.55-4.75 μm band
minimize mean transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm band
minimize mean transmittance in 4.85-5.20 μm band
manufacturing_considerations: ZnS and MgF2 are conventional depositable IR dielectrics
thickness tolerances should reflect the perturbation ranges used in optimization
theory_basis: Quarter-wave optical thickness creates maximum reflectance at design wavelength through constructive interference of partial reflections
High/low index contrast (ZnS ~2.3, MgF2 ~1.35 in mid-IR) determines stopband width and reflectance per pair
Dual-passband filters require envelope modulation beyond simple periodic stacks
Front layers dominate fine phase relationships; rear layers influence spectral envelope shape
Recalled from standard thin-film optics design practice, not from checked sources
expected_advantages: Two-tier perturbation may escape local optima that uniform perturbation cannot
Decoupling phase and envelope tuning could better separate the two narrow passbands
Maintains same material pair and layer count as prior iterations for fair comparison
Builds on iteration_08 baseline which achieved 0.698 target score
known_risks: ZnS and MgF2 refractive indices in 4-5 μm range are recalled approximations; actual dispersion data from registry will determine true performance
Daimon-20 substrate index at these wavelengths is recalled as ~1.42 but registry data is authoritative
The 478.0/815.0 nm baseline comes from iteration_08 candidate 1, not from independent quarter-wave calculation at band centers
±3% and ±12% perturbation bounds are heuristic choices; optimal ranges are unknown without literature
22 layers may be insufficient for sharp dual-band separation; 24 layers might perform better but this route fixes 22 for consistency
execution_request_english: Design a 22-layer alternating multilayer infrared filter on CaF2 (Daimon-20) substrate for dual-band transmission. Stack sequence from air ambient: ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2 (22 layers total). Optimize individual layer thicknesses with two-tier perturbation: layers 1-12 constrained to ±3% variation around baseline thicknesses of 478.0 nm (ZnS) and 815.0 nm (MgF2) alternating; layers 13-22 allowed ±12% independent variation. Spectral range 3500-5300 nm. Target: maximize mean transmittance in passbands 4150-4350 nm and 4550-4750 nm; minimize mean transmittance in stopbands 3600-4000 nm and 4850-5200 nm. Normal incidence, coherent thin-film calculation. No metal layers. Materials resolved from registry as zns, mgf2, and CaF2 (Daimon-20).
revision_reason: Refinement per feedback directives: applying two-tier perturbation scheme to layers 1-12 (±3% around iteration_08 candidate 1 baseline) and layers 13-22 (±12% independent) to resolve fine-scale phase mismatches and spectral envelope adjustments while maintaining the same control axis. Repaired material name from ambiguous CaF2 to specific Daimon-20 dataset.
